paper: Kojevnikov & Song, 'Some impossibility results for inference with cluster dependence with large clusters' (arXiv:2109.03971v4, Jun 2023; J. Econometrics 2023)
how_read: Full PDF text extracted (38 pp); keyword scan of whole text for ~45 terms; read abstract, intro, Sec 3-4 theorem statements (Thm 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, Cor 3.1, 4.1, 4.2); proofs (Sec 7 lemmas) not read line by line
nearest_statement: Asymptotic impossibility: with one large cluster the mean cannot be consistently discriminated (Thm 3.1/Cor 3.1); >=2 large clusters suffice via IM-type t-test (Thm 3.2); long-run variance consistently estimable iff sum n_m^2/n^2 -> 0 (Thm 4.1). Normal/dependency-graph models, asymptotic, no finite-population sampling, no finite-sample critical values.

paper: Mueller, 'A More Robust t-Test' (arXiv:2007.07065v1 Jul 2020 + author-page version Nov 2022 = revised REStat-stage draft; REStat published version not obtained)
how_read: Full PDF text of both versions extracted (57 and 64 pp); keyword scan of whole text; read abstract, intro, Sec 4.2 nuisance-space definition, simulation design; proofs/appendices not read line by line
nearest_statement: Extreme-value + normal approximation test for iid / two-sample / clustered regression; size control checked numerically via importance sampling over a nuisance space (Sec 4.2 restrictions (a)-(h): tail index <1/2, sum of squared middle observations <=2). 'Two-point' there = least-favourable prior over nuisance parameters, not two-point populations. Sampling is iid (with replacement) from CPS/HMDA subpopulations. No finite-sample certified critical values over a bounded max|x-mean|/SD class.

paper: Hagemann, 'Permutation inference with a finite number of heterogeneous clusters' (arXiv:1907.01049v2, Feb 2023; REStat 2023)
how_read: Full PDF text extracted (29 pp); keyword scan of whole text; read abstract, intro, Sec 2 (Thm 2.1, Cor 2.2), Thm 3.2 statement; appendix proofs not read
nearest_statement: Thm 2.1: for independent symmetric heterogeneous-scale variables the level-adjusted permutation test using the second-largest permutation statistic has exact size sup = 1/2^{min(q1,q2)} (so q>=4 gives 6.25%); Cor 2.2 extends to symmetric scale mixtures. Sign/permutation-group counting (finite-sample, requires symmetry + independence), the classical log2(1/alpha)-type threshold in number of clusters; no finite population, no strata design variance shares, no bounded-ratio class.
theorem_number: Thm 2.1, Cor 2.2 (nearest to B only as the sign-flip 2^-q baseline)

paper: Poetscher & Preinerstorfer, 'Valid heteroskedasticity robust testing' (arXiv:2104.12597v3, Jul 2023; Econometric Theory 2023)
how_read: Full PDF text extracted (93 pp); keyword scan (incl. 13 'leverage' hits, 283 'critical value' hits) of whole text; read abstract, intro, Sec 5 (Thm 5.1, discussion of Bakirov-Szekely/IM variants), Thm 6.4, Thm A.5 statements; Sec 11 simulations and appendix proofs not read in full
nearest_statement: Gaussian (or scale-mixture) linear regression with unrestricted heteroskedasticity class C_Het: Thm 5.1 gives sufficient (and in places necessary) conditions (e_i not in span(X) on I1, i.e. no extreme leverage h_ii=1) for existence of a finite size-controlling critical value, and the smallest one; Thm A.5 does the same for clustered covariance classes C(n1..nm). Structurally an 'exists iff no degenerate configuration' result, but over covariance structures in a parametric Gaussian model, with no finite-population sampling, no equivariant bounded interval, no knapsack/box-class frontier.
theorem_number: Thm 5.1, Thm 6.4, Thm A.5 (structural analogue of A only)

paper: Ibragimov & Mueller 2010 JBES 't-statistic based correlation and heterogeneity robust inference' (author-page PDF tstat.pdf, accepted/final version, 16 pp)
how_read: Full PDF text extracted and keyword-scanned; read abstract, Sec 2 incl. Thm 1 (Bakirov-Szekely) and Thm 2 in full; Monte Carlo sections skimmed; extended HIER version (SSRN 964224) not read
nearest_statement: Thm 1: for independent Gaussians with arbitrary heterogeneous variances the usual two-sided t-test is valid for alpha <= 2*Phi(-sqrt3)=0.0833 and all q>=2 (and for alpha<=0.1 with 2<=q<=14); sup attained at k equal variances and rest zero (extremal configuration analogous in spirit to two-point/knapsack structure but Gaussian). Thm 2: UMP scale-invariant optimality. Gaussianity of group estimators assumed; no distribution-free finite-sample critical values over a bounded-share class.

POMI 328; J Math Sci 139:6497) -- ORIGINAL NOT OBTAINED (mathnet.ru returned 403; publisher paywalled); read instead Szekely, 'Student's t-test for scale mixture errors' (arXiv math/0610838, Lehmann Symposium 2006, 7 pp) in full, plus IM10 Thm 1 and abstracts of the original (Springer/mathnet)
how_read: Szekely arXiv paper read in full (all 7 pages); original Bakirov-Szekely only via abstracts and its restatement in IM10 Thm 1, Szekely Thm 3.1/Cor 1, PP Sec 1/5.2
nearest_statement: Szekely Thm 2.1: for symmetric scale-mixture-of-Rademacher errors, 2^{-ceil(a^2)} <= 1-t^S_{n-1}(a) = m/2^n (m = max vertices of the n-cube covered by a ball of radius sqrt(n-a^2)); Thm 3.1/Cor 1-2: for Gaussian scale mixtures sup over scales attained with k equal nonzero scales, usual t critical value valid for a>=sqrt3; Table 1 gives certified critical values for t^G_n. This is certified critical values and extremal configurations for a t-interval over a distribution class (symmetric / GSM), so analogous to K, but the class is defined by symmetry/scale-mixture, not by a bound on max|x-mean|/SD or on the largest share of one value in the sum of squares, and populations are random errors, not fixed finite populations. K not contained exactly.
theorem_number: Thm 2.1, Thm 3.1, Cor 1, Cor 2, Table 1 (Szekely arXiv); IM10 Thm 1
